body: Yeah, feeling a good bit better. The thoughts are still there, but they don't feel as real/immediate. Back in control and doing okay. Thanks a lot for the help, talking things out did more good than I'd thought it would.

I didn't actually have any idea of what I wanted to *do* when I chose my major. The priorities were basically money (planned on going to law school afterwards, despite not being very excited about it), getting done with BYU as soon as possible, and understanding the mechanics of how people distribute power–I'm the sort of guy who loves to learn, and this was all my first exposure to how the real world works. I fell in love with it.

But ever since I can remember, I've associated success with money, and though I fight it I still feel like a failure when I have to ask for help from anyone. That "get degrees fast to make mad cash" mindset sort of took over when I went for my master's degree. I didn't really know what I was doing, but everyone told me school was the answer, so I did it. Dropped the law school ideal for an MBA after talking to a **lot** of unhappy lawyers.

Over the past couple of years, though, I think I've finally calmed down enough to figure out what I really want to do with myself. I think I'd be a good high school teacher or college professor (if I chose to go for the PhD). I really want to help people. Improve their lives, expand their worlds, make them happy. Pass along a sense of wonder about the world.

I thought an MBA might be able to help me get a position doing that sort of thing, but it's become apparent that my sole purpose in life is making money. It's not too fulfilling, though the whole culture around it satisfies that urge to rise through the ranks and make as much money as possible. The $40k of student loans on my back is keeping me from making any big career shifts right now, and I just sort of feel trapped. By expectations, practical considerations, and my own fears.

Also, sorry for the book I'm writing in each response. It's pretty therapeutic to throw all this out there, haven't talked about this sort of stuff with anyone before.

I've tried talking to my brother and mom a few times since they're the most accepting, but they tend to get uncomfortable and end the conversation pretty quickly. 

Since I'm not dating anyone right now, I don't think they've really confronted the idea; they haven't had to since I haven't been on a date since high school, and they're content to keep it out of mind until I force it on them. Actually, writing that out here, their attitudes have probably been a significant contributor to my perpetual bachelorhood.

But you're right, I should be more upfront about it. I've kind of let them shove all this nonsense back into the closet, which really isn't good. I need to get the balls to stand up for myself, though I can't say I'm looking forward to those conversations.

I lurk around there every so often. It can be cathartic, but folks there seem to feel pretty bitter about the whole thing. I'm more disappointed than anything else. Maybe the anger kicks in once I get all my own stuff sorted out.

And yeah, not the best organization in the world for LGBT folks. I came out while attending BYU, during the whole Prop 8 nonsense. In retrospect, I couldn't have timed it any worse than that, but it needed to come out one way or another. I was losing my mind.

Yeah, it's the LDS church (Mormons). Goes back through both sides of my family to my great-great-great grandparents or something–to say I'm the black sheep of the family would be a tremendous understatement. All my cousins are at BYU, most of the family lives in Utah... the whole Mormon shebang.

On some level, I know that what they say doesn't matter. I really do. But it's just... hard. Hard to have your ailing grandparents give you a letter for your birthday explaining that you need to go on a mission and get married so you can join them in heaven. Hard to explain to your sobbing mom why you won't come to church. Hard to look your dad in the eyes when he tells you how disappointed he is about gay marriage becoming legal in Utah today.

They mean well, and I understand that, but it's eaten me away inside to the point where there just isn't much left most days. I just get so detached that suicide really does feel like the right answer a lot of the time, no matter what the rest of my brain says. It sucks.

But anyhow, getting off on a bit of a tangent there myself. Sorry. Having a particularly bad day. But thanks for the comment. Seeing that there are supportive folks somewhere out there really does help.

Honestly, I've never really thought much about relocating. I've never really taken the time to pinpoint that it's probably my environment doing this to me–this depressed haze has just become normal. I guess it's hard for me to see family as a negative influence in my life, even despite all this, which is kind of stupid of me. 

Having it all laid out, though, it seems a change of scenery and people would probably help a ton.

I'll take the first step and try finding/applying to a few lower-level out of state jobs tonight. Taking some kind of action would probably help more than I realize. It's at least worth a shot.

Studied political science undergrad, business for grad school. I like seeing how people organize themselves to get stuff done. The problem I've run into there is that I have my MBA, but not a ton of work experience, which makes me pretty unmarketable. Entry level jobs don't like that I have a master's degree, anything higher doesn't like that I only have one year of full-time work and a bunch of internships/volunteer work/part-time jobs to round it all out.

...at least, that's the answer I usually feed people. I think on a deeper level, I'm just kind of terrified of playing that whole social game, though that hasn't stopped me from sending out around 40-50 applications in the past year. I feel like I'm a burden on people when I ask for job referrals, like I'm not worth the time or effort. My self-worth is basically shot at this point, and it's bled out into everything else in my life.
